title: Casper and the Garden
premise: Xanthe Dunmore poisons herself for a living as the king's food-taster while secretly peddling outlawed charms to survive. When a feral child arrives at her door speaking the First Tongue — the language that once commanded dragons — Xanthe discovers the child is the last vessel of dragon-fire, and the 'king' she serves is a hollowed man puppeted by an ancient parasite wearing the crown. Hunted by the crown's witch-hunters and betrayed by her own fence, Xanthe must choose between the immunity she has built and the magic she has hidden, ultimately unbinding the king in a rite that costs the child's fire and forces the city to reckon with justice no law ever wrote.
about_author: Cyrus Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people caught in machinery of power, and live quietly where no one asks about their past.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She survives a poisoned banquet through her engineered immunity, then slips home to sell a luck-charm to a desperate laundress, showing the double life she leads under the Edict of Ash. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness — she trusts no one, including herself.

chapters.title: A Knock in the First Tongue
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A soot-streaked child appears at her door speaking a language that makes her hidden charms hum and answer. The child, Casper, carries a dying coal of dragon-fire in his chest and knows her true name. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. He shows Xanthe a vision: the king is an empty vessel, and something older than kingdoms speaks through his mouth, signing death warrants with his hand. Emotional beat: horror — the law Xanthe feared is a mask over something worse.

chapters.title: The Fence's Price
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She turns to her charm-broker, Merrick, for help smuggling Casper out — and he sells her to the witch-hunters to buy his own pardon. Xanthe and Casper flee through the ash-market as her stall burns. Emotional beat: betrayal; the underground she trusted is a trap.

chapters.title: Immunity
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, hiding in the old tanneries. She realizes her three years of poison have made her the only person the parasite's magic cannot grip — her body refuses enchantment. Casper begins teaching her the First Tongue. Emotional beat: dawning purpose; her damage is her armor.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and hunter-captain Veyra's POV. Veyra, a true believer in the Edict, corners them; Xanthe uses a forbidden charm openly to escape, saving Casper but becoming exactly the criminal the law says she is. Emotional beat: crossing the line — no way back to her old life.

chapters.title: The King's Hollow Voice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She infiltrates the palace through the kitchens she knows intimately and meets the king alone: a flickering, exhausted man who begs her, in half-remembered words, to end it. Emotional beat: pity — the tyrant is also the first victim.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the throne room before the whole court, she begins the rite, speaking the First Tongue as the parasite fights back through edicts, guards, and Merrick's testimony. Casper's fire gutters to a single coal. Emotional beat: terror and resolve at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, Xanthe and Casper's alternating POV. The parasite abandons the king and tries to take Casper as a newer vessel; Xanthe lets it grip her — and her poisoned blood burns it from the inside. The king is freed; Casper's fire is spent saving her. Emotional beat: sacrifice and reversal — the taster poisons the poisoner.

chapters.title: What Grows After Ash
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, weeks later. The Edict collapses with the parasite's death; Veyra chooses justice over law and testifies. Casper, fireless but free, plants a garden in the ash-market with Xanthe, where the first magic allowed openly is a seed-charm. Emotional beat: quiet renewal — identity rebuilt, power returned to the people.
